verdict.rationale: Mailchimp Transactional (formerly Mandrill) is documented as a separate API/SMTP product for event-driven messages. It has its own rejection allowlist/denylist and dedicated IPs, which gives it separate suppression and reputation controls. The pack never documents transactional templates or states that a receipt reaches a contact who unsubscribed from marketing, and one user reports a marketing-email complaint shutting off their Mandrill inbound support email, which casts doubt on full isolation. missing for 10: documented transactional-specific templates, explicit statement that marketing unsubscribes don't suppress transactional sends, documented reputation isolation between marketing and transactional, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, transactional email is kept separate from marketing — its own templates, suppression rules, and reputation — so a receipt still delivers to an unsubscribed contact

citations.quote: Mailchimp Transactional (formerly Mandrill) sends targeted and event-driven messages via the API or SMTP, fast—with best-in-class deliverability.
Adds an email to your email rejection allowlist. If the address is currently on your denylist, that denylist entry will be removed automatically.
Requests an additional dedicated IP for your account.
